public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 549

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/549](https://www.erdosproblems.com/549)
- [Bu74] Burr, S. A., Generalized Ramsey theory for graphs—a survey. Graphs and combinatorics
  (Proc. Capital Conf., George Washington Univ., Washington, D.C., 1973) (1974), 52-75.
- [NSZ16] S. Norin and Y. R. Sun and Y. Zhao, Asymptotics of Ramsey numbers of double stars.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos549

/--
If $T$ is a tree which is a bipartite graph with $k$ vertices in one class and $2k$ vertices
in the other class then
$$R(T)=4k-1.$$

This is false: Norin, Sun, and Zhao [NSZ16] have proved that if $T$ is the union of two stars on $k$
and $2k$ vertices, with an edge joining the centre of the two stars, then $R(T)\geq (4.2-o(1))k$,
and conjectured that $R(T)=(4.2+o(1))k$.

This problem is #15 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_549 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin k ⊕ Fin (2 * k))),
      T.IsTree →
      (∀ x₁ x₂, ¬ T.Adj (Sum.inl x₁) (Sum.inl x₂)) →
      (∀ y₁ y₂, ¬ T.Adj (Sum.inr y₁) (Sum.inr y₂)) →
      SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey T = 4 * k - 1 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos549

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly restricts k to k ≥ 2, whereas the cited question describes bipartition sizes k and 2k without this restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted cases add no constraint. At k = 0 there is no connected, nonempty tree. At k = 1 the tree and bipartition hypotheses force K_{1,2}, whose diagonal Ramsey number is 3 = 4k − 1. Thus the universal formula over all natural k is equivalent to the formula over k ≥ 2, as are their negations. This equivalence, including the Ramsey-number calculation for k = 1, was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: S. Norin, Y. R. Sun and Y. Zhao, Asymptotics of Ramsey numbers of double stars (2016), arXiv:1605.03612. Read the LaTeX source, especially §1 (the Ramsey definition, Theorem 1.3, and the explicit k,2k question and counterexample) and §6: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1605.03612.

S. A. Burr, Generalized Ramsey theory for graphs—a survey, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 406 (1974), 52–75. Read the publisher's abstract and bibliographic information; the full chapter required subscription access: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0066435.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully records the negative answer. NSZ16 explicitly states that T = S(2k−1,k−1) has bipartition sizes k and 2k and Ramsey number at least 4.2k−o(k), disproving 4k−1. Checked the scope of answer(False), ordinary rather than induced graph containment, tree semantics, vertex counts, natural subtraction, and isomorphism invariance. The Ramsey infimum has a nonempty defining set by finite Ramsey theory. Lean checks also exhibited an eligible tree at k = 2. The Erdős Problems webpage returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the exact claim and its disproof were independently available in the cited NSZ16 paper. The reviewed file still matches the specified commit.
